spec.comment: The `sorted(iterable)` lowering of the dynamic-language frontends (py-sh-go) emits echo "$(printf '%s\n' "$arr[@]" | sort [-n] [-u] | awk join)" — a SPAWN pipeline whose sort/awk stages exist only to order and join an ARRAY THE PROGRAM ALREADY HAS IN MEMORY. That is pure in-memory compute expressed as three subprocesses; every backend can lower it natively (JS: Array.sort; C: qsort; Go: sort.Slice; Perl: sort). The node carries the whole pipeline as ONE contract expression so no backend has to re-recognize the shape.

values.comment: the array value expression (the printf %s\n argument — today an IrExpr::Call{func:"param", args:["slice", arr, "@", ""]} or equivalent whole-array read)

numeric.comment: sort -n: numeric ordering (sort -n -u from the lowering)

required: %s",", "}{printf "%s",$0}' stage — today ", "; empty string = newline-per-line passthrough)

manifest.name: sort-uniq-pipeline
manifest.invariant: ONLY the exact pipeline shape printf '%s\n' ARRAY | sort [-n|-u]... | [awk join] lifts (the py-sh-go sorted() lowering); a pipeline with ANY other stage, any flag outside {-n,-u}, a custom sort key (-k/-t), a non-trivial awk program (anything beyond the comma-join printf pair), stdin/redirect noise, or a non-whole-array printf argument REFUSES (open node model, refuse > guess). The lift is status-preserving (printf/sort/awk all succeed on the fixed inputs; lastExit 0) and byte-preserving for the emitted string (LC_ALL=C ordering — the shell sort's default locale is the contract; a backend whose native sort differs MUST sort under the C collation to stay oracle-equal).
